## Project Overview

Jarvis is an emotion-aware voice assistant demo built around a browser conversation
console and a FastAPI backend. The system accepts text or recorded speech, detects
the user's emotional state, retrieves persona-specific response guidance, sends a
context-rich prompt to an LLM, stores the turn in session memory, and returns both a
text reply and a generated speech artifact when TTS is available.

The project is designed as a working prototype for emotionally adaptive assistant
behavior rather than a generic chatbot. The core design idea is that Jarvis should
not only answer the user's words; it should adjust tone, pacing, and practical next
steps based on detected emotion, recent conversation history, persona preference,
and optional wellness signals.

## Tech Stack

| Layer | Technology | Use In This Project |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Language | Python 3.11 / 3.12 | Backend application, services, scripts, and tests |
| Web framework | FastAPI | REST API, websocket endpoint, app lifecycle, and static UI route |
| ASGI server | Uvicorn | Local development server for the FastAPI app |
| Data validation | Pydantic, pydantic-settings | Request/response schemas and environment-backed configuration |
| Database ORM | SQLAlchemy async | Conversation memory persistence |
| Primary database | MySQL with `aiomysql` | Main configured database target |
| Fallback database | SQLite with `aiosqlite` | Local fallback when MySQL is unavailable |
| Frontend | HTML, CSS, vanilla JavaScript | Browser conversation console at `/ui` |
| Browser audio | MediaRecorder API, Web Audio API | Microphone recording, audio preview, and UI cue tones |
| Wake phrase | Web Speech API | Browser-side wake phrase listening where supported |
| LLM providers | AWS Bedrock, Groq, local deterministic mode | Assistant response generation |
| Speech-to-text | OpenAI Whisper package | Legacy voice transcription |
| Audio emotion | Hugging Face Transformers | Wav2Vec2-based emotion classification when dependencies are available |
| Voice understanding | SenseVoice / FunASR / ModelScope | Optional combined transcript, emotion, language, and audio event path |
| Text-to-speech | Coqui TTS | Assistant speech synthesis when installed |
| Prompt assets | Plain text prompt templates | Runtime prompt assembly for Jarvis responses |
| Persona guidance | JSON cache files | Precomputed persona and emotion response guidance |
| Demo assets | JSON scenarios and generated WAV files | Repeatable presentation and smoke-test flows |

## Product Experience

The main user experience is the browser UI at `/ui`, implemented with plain HTML,
CSS, and JavaScript in `app/static/`.

The intended product flow is persona-first. The user selects the assistant persona or
support style at the start of the session, before recording or sending a message.
That selected `persona_id` is then included with each text or voice turn so Jarvis can
combine the user's detected emotion with the chosen persona and reply accordingly.

Primary user workflows:

- Select the persona/profile for the conversation at the start of the product flow.
- Start a text conversation with `/api/chat`.
- Record a browser microphone clip after persona selection and send it to `/api/voice`.
- Use an optional transcript override to bypass Whisper during demos.
- Simulate wellness signals with heart rate and stress level controls.
- Listen for the wake phrase `Hey JayJay` or `Hey Jay Jay`.
- Play back the latest assistant audio response when a `.wav` is generated.
- Review the conversation thread stored for the active session.
- Inspect transcript, assistant response, emotion details, output artifact, and raw
  JSON diagnostics.
- Clear the current session with the new conversation action.

The UI is intentionally diagnostic. It presents both the polished conversation
surface and the underlying metadata so the emotional pipeline can be explained
during demos.

## Visual Design

The frontend uses a dark, futuristic console style to support the Jarvis theme:

- Typeface pairing:
  - `Space Grotesk` for readable interface text.
  - `Orbitron` for machine-like labels and mood headings.
- Layout:
  - A centered `shell` with a hero area followed by functional panels.
  - Responsive grids for controls, media, diagnostics, and history.
  - Conversation history uses role-based cards aligned left/right for assistant/user
    turns.
- Components:
  - Emotion monitor with mood title, summary, glowing core, animated rings, and
    waveform bars.
  - Controls panel for session, transcript override, wellness simulation, text input,
    and conversation actions.
  - Media panel for recorded clip preview and assistant output playback.
  - Diagnostics panel for transcript, reply, emotion debug payload, artifact path,
    and raw response JSON.

Emotion themes are implemented with CSS variables on `body[data-emotion]`:

| Emotion | Visual Treatment |
| --- | --- |
| `neutral` / `calm` | Cool blue baseline, slower waveform, lower pulse height |
| `happy` / `excited` / `surprised` | Brighter green/yellow energy, faster waveform |
| `sad` | Softer blue palette, slower pulse, lower waveform |
| `fear` | Warm orange alert state, faster waveform, higher pulse |
| `angry` | Red high-alert state, fastest waveform, strongest pulse |

The visual state is not decorative only. It is meant to make emotion detection
visible to the user and useful during demos.

## System Architecture

High-level request flow:

```text
Persona selected at session start
  -> browser text or microphone input
  -> FastAPI route
  -> optional speech-to-text
  -> emotion detection
  -> session memory lookup
  -> persona guidance lookup
  -> prompt context assembly
  -> LLM response generation
  -> TTS or text artifact output
  -> memory persistence
  -> browser UI update
```

## System Flowchart

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    A[User opens /ui browser console] --> A1[Select persona / support style]

    B -->|Text message| C[POST /api/chat with persona_id]

    D --> E[POST /api/voice with persona_id + audio]
    E --> F[Save uploaded audio]

    F --> G{Voice understanding mode}
    G -->|legacy| H[Whisper transcription]
    H --> I[Hybrid emotion detection]
    I --> I1[Audio classifier]
    I --> I2[Transcript keyword scoring]
    I1 --> J[Choose final emotion]
    I2 --> J

    G -->|SenseVoice optional| K[SenseVoice transcript + emotion metadata]
    K --> J

    C --> L[Resolve selected persona]
    J --> L
    L --> M[Load recent session history]
    M --> N[Load persona + emotion guidance cache]
    N --> O[Build prompt context payload]
    O --> P{LLM provider}
    P -->|Bedrock| Q[Generate assistant reply]
    P -->|Groq| Q
    P -->|Local deterministic| Q

    Q --> R[Generate TTS or text artifact]
    R --> S[Persist user + assistant turns]
    S --> T[Return ChatResponse JSON]
    T --> U[Update transcript, reply, mood, history, diagnostics, and audio playback]
```

| --- | --- | --- |
| App entry | `main.py`, `app/api.py` | FastAPI app creation, routes, startup/shutdown, static file mounting |
| Config | `app/config.py` | Environment-backed settings for providers, models, storage, and audio paths |
| Orchestration | `app/services/orchestrator.py` | Coordinates chat and voice pipelines |
| LLM | `app/services/llm.py` | Builds prompts and calls Bedrock, Groq, or local deterministic mode |

| STT | `app/services/stt.py` | Whisper transcription path |
| SenseVoice | `app/services/sensevoice.py` | Optional unified voice understanding path |
| TTS | `app/services/tts.py` | Coqui TTS synthesis with text artifact fallback |
| Memory | `app/services/memory.py` | Stores and retrieves recent session turns |
| Persona guidance | `app/services/rag.py` | Loads persona metadata and cached emotion guidance |
| Data models | `app/models.py`, `app/schemas.py` | SQLAlchemy table and Pydantic API contracts |
| Frontend | `app/static/index.html`, `app/static/app.js`, `app/static/styles.css` | Browser conversation console |

## Backend Design

The backend is centered on `AssistantOrchestrator`. Routes stay thin and delegate
work to the orchestration layer.

The selected persona is part of the request contract. The frontend should capture the
persona at the beginning of the session and send that `persona_id` with both text and
voice requests. The backend then combines the selected persona with detected emotion
to pick the correct guidance before the LLM reply is generated.

Text chat path:

1. `POST /api/chat` receives `ChatRequest`, including the selected `persona_id`.
2. The orchestrator resolves the selected persona metadata.
3. If no emotion was supplied, text keyword emotion detection runs.
4. Recent turns for the session are loaded from memory.
5. `LLMService` builds a prompt with emotion, persona, history, and wellness context.
6. The selected LLM provider generates a reply.
7. `TextToSpeechService` attempts speech synthesis or writes a text fallback.
8. User and assistant turns are stored in the database.
9. `ChatResponse` is returned to the UI.

Voice path:

1. The user selects a persona first, then records the voice turn.
2. `POST /api/voice` accepts multipart audio plus session, selected persona, and demo
   fields.
3. The uploaded file is saved under the configured uploads directory.
4. If SenseVoice is enabled, it can produce transcript and emotion metadata together.
5. In legacy mode, Whisper transcribes audio and `EmotionService` combines audio and
   transcript-based emotion signals.
6. The resulting transcript, selected persona, and emotion are passed into the normal
   chat path.
7. The response includes the transcript, detected emotion, debug payload, audio path,
   and optional wellness signal.

## API Design

Current API surface:

| Endpoint | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /` | Basic app status message |
| `GET /ui` | Browser console |
| `GET /health` | Provider status for LLM, STT, emotion, TTS, and database |
| `POST /api/chat` | Text turn |
| `POST /api/voice` | Voice upload turn |
| `GET /api/personas` | Available persona profiles |
| `GET /api/history/{session_id}` | Recent turns for a session |
| `DELETE /api/history/{session_id}` | Clear one session |
| `WS /ws/chat` | Minimal websocket path using neutral emotion and no memory |

The API response shape is designed for both user experience and debugging. A normal
chat response includes the user message, assistant message, detected emotion, optional
transcript, optional emotion debug payload, output artifact path, persona id, and
wellness signal.

## Data And Memory Design

Conversation memory is stored in the `conversation_turns` table:

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Primary key |
| `session_id` | Browser/demo session partition |
| `role` | `user` or `assistant` |
| `content` | Turn text |
| `emotion` | Emotion associated with the turn |
| `created_at` | Server timestamp |

The memory service retrieves the most recent turns for a session in chronological
order after querying newest-first. The current UI and prompt flow use up to 12 turns.

Database behavior:

- MySQL is the primary configured database.
- SQLite is used as a fallback when MySQL is unavailable and fallback is enabled.
- On app startup, all conversation history is currently cleared for demo cleanliness.

## Emotion Design

Emotion is used in three places:

- Backend response generation through prompt context and guidance.
- Frontend visual state through `body[data-emotion]`.
- Diagnostics through `emotion_debug` metadata.

Supported or planned emotion labels:

- `neutral`
- `calm`
- `happy`
- `excited`
- `surprised`
- `sad`
- `fear`
- `angry`
- `disgust`

Text emotion detection uses keyword groups for positive, sad, angry, and fear/stress
signals. Legacy voice mode combines audio model output with transcript keyword
signals. The hybrid design favors transcript emotion when the audio result is weak,
neutral/calm with a strong text cue, or clearly lower confidence than the text cue.

## Persona Guidance Design

Jarvis uses persona-aware guidance so different user profiles can receive different
response styles for the same emotion.

The product selection order is:

1. Choose the persona/profile at the start of the session.
2. Record or type the user turn.
3. Detect the user's emotion from text/audio signals.
4. Retrieve guidance using `selected persona + detected emotion`.
5. Generate a reply that matches both the persona preference and the user's current
   emotional state.

Current persona metadata lives in `corpus/personas.json`:

| Persona | Design Role |
| --- | --- |
| `tony_stark` | Direct, autonomy-respecting, low-emotion fixer |
| `maya_chen` | Soft, validating reassurance seeker |
| `uncle_ray` | Grounded, practical realist |
| `sam_rivera` | Warm reframer with emotional nuance |
| `priya_shah` | Stressed MSBA student needing pressure relief and tactics |
| `default_danny` | Warm, clear, grounded default |

Runtime guidance is loaded from `corpus/persona_guidance.json` by
`persona_id + detected_emotion`. This behaves like a precomputed RAG cache: the
assistant gets targeted style guidance without performing vector search or extra LLM
calls during the user turn.

## Prompt Design

The main prompt template is `prompts/jarvis_chat.txt`.

The prompt receives a JSON context payload containing:

- `user_text`
- `emotion`
- `detected_emotion`
- `emotion_guidance`
- `user_profile`
- `conversation_history`
- `wellness_signal`

Prompt rules emphasize:

- Answer directly in Jarvis' voice.
- Use context only when relevant.
- Adapt tone based on detected emotion, guidance, and user profile.
- Keep responses simple, practical, concise, and easy to say out loud.
- Support distress without diagnosing medical or mental health conditions.
- Avoid inventing personal facts not present in context.

## Model And Provider Design

The backend supports multiple provider modes:

| Layer | Current Design |
| --- | --- |
| LLM | Bedrock by default, Groq as alternate, local deterministic mode for offline tests |
| STT | Whisper in legacy voice mode |
| Audio emotion | Hugging Face wav2vec2 emotion classifier when dependencies are available |
| Unified voice understanding | Optional SenseVoice path |
| TTS | Coqui TTS when installed, text artifact fallback otherwise |
| Database | MySQL primary, SQLite fallback |

The `local` LLM provider is intentionally deterministic so smoke tests can verify the
pipeline without external credentials or network dependencies.

## Demo Design

The demo experience is designed to be repeatable and explainable:

- `demo/scenarios.json` provides scripted cases.
- `demo/audio/` contains generated WAV clips for voice endpoint tests.
- The UI includes transcript override for quick demos when local STT is unavailable.
- Wellness controls simulate future wearable input without requiring hardware.
- Diagnostics expose the exact JSON returned by the backend.
- Playback speed defaults to `1.25x` for faster presentation pacing.

## Safety And Reliability Design

Important safeguards and reliability choices:

- Provider health is exposed through `/health`.
- Placeholder API keys are treated as missing config.
- Empty string config values are normalized to `None`.
- LLM provider failures return structured errors.
- TTS gracefully falls back to a text artifact when audio synthesis is unavailable.
- Database initialization falls back to SQLite when configured.
- The assistant prompt explicitly avoids diagnosis and unsupported personal memory.
- The app clears stored history on startup to keep demos predictable.

## Current Limitations

- The wake phrase depends on browser Web Speech API support.
- The websocket endpoint is minimal and does not use full memory/emotion orchestration.
- Real-time streaming voice is configured as a future possibility but not wired into
  the current FastAPI flow.
- `disgust` is recognized as a planned/supported label in design docs, but the current
  UI falls back to neutral styling unless a dedicated theme is added.
- Persona guidance is cache-based rather than a live vector retrieval system.
- Conversation history is not durable across app restarts because startup clears it.

## Future Design Direction

Likely next design steps:

- Make the persona selector the first visible control in the browser UI and keep the
  selected persona visible during recording.
- Add a dedicated `disgust` visual theme and guidance checks.
- Make durable memory optional through a config flag.
- Promote the emotion/persona guidance cache into a true retrieval pipeline if the
  guidance set grows beyond the current matrix.
- Add richer emotion metrics such as valence, arousal, dominance, uncertainty, and
  mixed-emotion scores.
- Expand realtime voice support using the existing realtime model setting.
- Add automated frontend checks for the main conversation flows.
